correctness.rationale: For each prime power and integer admissible parameters, annihilator duality reduces to k<=n/2. For each distance t between selected k-subspaces, explicit linear-algebra constructions realize all four possible third-vertex adjacency patterns for t=1,2, and precisely three patterns for t>=3; the missing fourth is excluded by an intersection-dimension inequality. A vertex-transitive three-round EF profile criterion, with the diagonal and equality cases included, converts these exhaustive extension patterns into the exact iff theorem. Explicit rank-two and rank-three separating sentences establish three distinct classes. Gaussian binomial monotonicity and boundary sizes 3,35,1395 prove the claimed sharp within-family bound. The direct full logical-type checker and finite-field/orbit checker both replayed successfully; universal correctness follows from the proof, not the finite enumeration.

A previous rank-three strongly regular result can cover the effective-rank-two Grassmann case, and Johnson logic results cover comparison representatives, but neither implies effective-rank-at-least-three Grassmann graphs nor the field-independent full three-class theorem. Six actual indexed literature queries returned geometric/spectral but no dominating logical result. The claim includes new uniform third-vertex constructions, and its prior implication risk is qualified by inaccessible/unindexed work.

value.rationale: This is an exact complete classification of the first-order rank-three theories of a canonical infinite family from finite geometry, uniformly in both subspace parameters and arbitrary field sizes/characteristics, not a narrow unmotivated slice. The constructive pair-orbit lemma identifies the precise structural reason why all field information is invisible at rank three. It proves sharp quantifier-rank thresholds, exact minimal Grassmann representatives including the sharp 1395-vertex uniform bound, and cross-family Johnson representatives useful for testing rank-three properties. Existing diameter-two/Johnson results do not render the higher-rank family classification a routine corollary.
